finish.immersive_jewelry.antique.descrip: Darkened recesses and old-world charm: takes enchantment far better and favours magic. Takes gunpowder for the patina.

handbook.immersive_jewelry.welcome.title: The Jeweler's Craft
handbook.immersive_jewelry.welcome.text:
Jewelry is made here, not crafted. A piece is its stones, its metal and the care you put into it.

Cut a stone on the Lapidary Wheel. Forge a blank. Set the stone by hand at the Jeweler's Bench and choose a finish. Then wear it: what it does comes from what it is made of, and how well.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.stones.title: Gemstones
handbook.immersive_jewelry.stones.text:
Diamonds, emeralds, amethyst, lapis and quartz are rough stones as they are; so are the gems of other mods. Rubies, sapphires, topaz and onyx also turn up rough in treasure and at the Jeweler.

When a stone first reaches the wheel it is appraised: its size, its clarity (few inclusions is better) and its luster. That character never changes.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wheel.title: The Lapidary Wheel
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wheel.text:
Place a stone on the wheel and use it again to choose a cut. Sneak with an empty hand to take the stone back.

A lap improves the wheel: an Emery Lap grinds faster and steadier, a Diamond Lap faster still, with wider facets and cooler stones. Laps wear with every cut.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.title: Cutting
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.text:
Move the mouse to press the stone against the wheel; hold the left button or Space to grind.

Keep the white diamond - where the wheel really touches, wobbling more the harder you press - on the brass facet. Release when the depth needle is inside the band. Grinding elsewhere scratches the stone; grinding past the band overcuts it.

Watch the heat: past its mark the stone chips. Pause to let it cool.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cuts.title: Choosing a Cut
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cuts.text:
Cabochon: four wide passes, very forgiving, kind to opaque stones, gentle in effect.
Round: six facets, balanced.
Emerald: long steps and fine corners; keeps more stone and its effects last longer.
Brilliant: ten facets, the strongest effect, the most waste and the most risk.

Hard stones grind slowly; brittle and included ones chip sooner.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.blanks.title: Blanks and Frames
handbook.immersive_jewelry.blanks.text:
The metal part of a piece is forged. With Immersive Smithing, a ring blank, amulet frame, bracelet blank or circlet frame is a small job at the Smith's Forge and Anvil, in any metal it knows. Your smithing quality is kept.

Without it, blanks are crafted from nuggets at a crafting table, with middling metalwork.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.title: The Jeweler's Bench
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.text:
Place a blank on the bench and use it with Jeweler's Pliers. Choose a design, the cut stones to set (all of one gem) and a finish. The stones wait on the bench while you work: close the screen and they come back to you.

The bench is also the Jeweler villager's workstation.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.title: Setting a Stone
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.text:
Prongs are pressed in a balanced order, each followed by its opposite. Hold to squeeze and release inside the brass band. The band follows the pressure on the opposite prong: match it and the stone sits level.

Too hard bends a prong (and may chip a brittle stone); too soft leaves it loose - squeeze once more. A bezel has more, gentler points and protects its stone.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.finishes.text:
Polished: brighter and stronger stones, a frame that wears sooner. Takes Polishing Compound.
Burnished: a tougher frame and steadier effects.
Antique: darker recesses, far better enchanting, a touch more magic. Takes gunpowder.

A finished piece can be refinished at the bench.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wearing.title: Wearing Jewelry
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wearing.text:
Rings, amulets, bracelets and circlets are worn in jewelry slots: two rings, one of each other form. With Curios they use its slots; otherwise open the jewelry slots from the ring button in your inventory or with J.

Your workmanship combines metalwork, the cut and the setting.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.effects.title: What Jewelry Does
handbook.immersive_jewelry.effects.text:
Each gem has a theme and each form expresses it differently. A ruby ring builds heat with every hit; a ruby amulet saves you when you are nearly beaten; a ruby bracelet rewards a charge.

The metal biases it (gold favours magic, silver protection, copper answers quickly), the cut sets its strength and steadiness, and the finish tunes it. Read a piece's tooltip for its numbers.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.care.title: Care and Repair
handbook.immersive_jewelry.care.text:
Jewelry does not wear in ordinary fighting, only under heavy blows. A worn frame can be repaired at the bench with a nugget of its metal, a little less fully after every rework.

Stones can be taken out again with the pliers, gently. A chipped stone is recut at the wheel, smaller but whole.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.designs.title: Designs
handbook.immersive_jewelry.designs.text: Solitaire and bezel rings, pendant and locket amulets, cuffs and simple circlets are known to every jeweler. Richer designs with three stones - the trilogy ring, halo amulet, link bracelet and diadem - are learned from Design Sketches, found in treasure or bought from Jewelers.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.jeweler.title: The Jeweler
handbook.immersive_jewelry.jeweler.text: A villager who claims a Jeweler's Bench becomes a Jeweler. Jewelers trade rough and cut stones, pliers, laps, sketches and, at the highest level, a piece of village work: good, but never a masterwork. That is yours to make.
